your_book:
Jaleel's book had a quiet but broadly positive Tuesday, September 22. The clearest winners were consumer names: On Holding (ONON, ~4% weight) surged +7.6% and AutoZone (AZO, ~6% weight) added +3.3% alongside a Nasdaq flirting with records and a fifth straight day of falling oil. Boston Scientific (BSX, ~9% weight) and Zoetis (ZTS, ~10% weight) also rallied meaningfully — +2.7% and +2.1% respectively — which matters given their combined size. The chip sleeve held up: NVDA (+0.7%) and AVGO (+0.5%) caught a tailwind from falling yields, lower oil, and Intel-SK Hynix manufacturing chatter. The one notable drag was Adobe (ADBE, ~5% weight), off -4.5%, which is an ironic twist — the session's positive catalyst was AI executives signaling growth may need to slow, which theoretically relieves competitive pressure on Adobe, yet the stock still sold off. That disconnect reinforces the existing risk flag: narrative fear, not fundamentals, is steering ADBE right now.

The drift problem in this book remains real and worth naming plainly. BSX carries an elevated guidance-cut flag (FY26 growth slashed to 7–8.5%) yet sits at the second-largest weight at ~9% and scored +2.7% today — price and thesis are moving in opposite directions temporarily. Same pattern in LULU (-18.9% unrealized, guidance cut, Americas comps -5% five quarters running) and RKLB (-8.1% unrealized, rated AVOID, nearly 7.5% of the book). A good day's price action doesn't resolve those structural tensions.

Watch the pharma cluster into October 22, when drug-pricing policy developments are next due. GILD, NVS, NBIX, and VRTX collectively represent meaningful weight, and MFN pricing pressure is a real overhang regardless of today's calm. ABT's earnings on October 13 are also worth flagging — the EPS guide has already been trimmed and a second miss would test the thesis on what is currently the second-largest position.

attention.note: RKLB has the lowest QARP score in the book (37.7), carries an AVOID verdict, is underwater, and is sized too large for a capital-preservation mandate — today's +3% day doesn't change the structural misfit.

attention.note: FY26 growth was slashed to 7–8.5% with management guiding flat through Q3, yet BSX remains ~8.8% of the book; the next read is October 28 and a second disappointment would be hard to absorb at this size.

attention.headline: Dropped -4.5% on a day when its sector tailwind was positive
attention.note: AI-slowdown commentary was supposed to be a relief for Adobe, yet the stock fell sharply anyway — narrative-driven selling that ignores fundamentals tends to persist, and the CFO exit plus ARR de-emphasis keep the story murky into December 8 earnings.

attention.note: The guidance cut is in place, tariffs are compressing margins, and China has stalled — the next catalyst isn't until December 9, leaving nearly 4% of the book exposed to continued drift with no near-term resolution.
